title: Fleet trade-in & leasing mix — commit timeline and decision triggers
content:
One-line summary:

Hybrid approach to preserve short-term capacity flexibility while minimizing long-run TCO: a rolling 26-week commit ladder that mixes leased increments and outright purchases with a managed trade-in window for aging hardware. Focus is on SKU diversification across regions and explicit triggers (utilization, price delta, lead-time signal) to convert leases to purchases or accelerate trade-ins.

Objectives:
- Avoid multi-quarter GPU shortfalls in US/EU during model launches.
- Keep peak utilization headroom >= 18% for burst patterns.
- Limit owned-capacity capex while keeping predictable baseline throughput.
- Use trade-in credits to lower refresh cost and shorten effective lead time for baseline fleets.

Key assumptions (baseline model):
- Quarterly demand growth: +9% Q/Q conservative estimate based on product roadmaps.
- Typical lead times: H100-80GB: 20 weeks nominal (range 16–28), A100-40GB: 14 weeks (10–20), L4-24GB: 8 weeks (4–12).
- Lease providers can deliver within 4–10 weeks for small bursts (<=200 units).
- Trade-in credit factor: 22–28% of purchase price if device returned within 30 months with certified burn < 20%.
- Target fleet mix (baseline owned+lease capacity): H100 45%, A100 35%, L4 20% weighted by effective performance units for inference.

SKU mix by region (current baseline units and target allocation):
- US: H100 2,400 (target 2,800), A100 1,200 (target 1,600), L4 600 (target 700).
- EU: H100 900 (target 1,050), A100 450 (target 600), L4 300 (target 350).
- APAC: H100 300 (target 450), A100 200 (target 260), L4 140 (target 180).

Short-term commit ladder (26-week rolling):
- Weeks 1–6: deploy leased burst pool (regional), target 600 units US, 200 EU, 100 APAC (mix skewed to L4 + A100 for latency-sensitive workloads).
- Weeks 7–14: finalize one purchase tranche (A100-heavy) sized to cover sustained demand after burst (US: +250 A100, EU: +100 A100).
- Weeks 15–26: evaluate H100 full-capacity purchase tranche based on utilization signal and vendor lead time hedge (order window opened if mean utilization > 72% over weeks 7–14).

Decision triggers (explicit):
- Lease->Buy conversion: triggered if rolling 4-week utilization > 70% and 8-week projected growth > 6% AND vendor lead time forecast <= 18 weeks.
- Accelerate trade-in: triggered if fleet age distribution shows > 32% units > 30 months in a region and maintenance incident rate spike > 1.3x baseline.
- Extend lease: when short-term price delta (lease cost vs spot purchase amortized) < 8% and lead time > 22 weeks.

Trade-in mechanics and economics:
- Expected trade-in credit: 25% purchase price on average, adjusted by SKU and burn rating. Credits can be applied against new committed purchase invoices within the same fiscal quarter.
- Trade-in timing: best ROI if executed in a 6–12 month window before full depreciation (24–36 months since purchase).
- Logistics: regional certified collection points (SFO, AMS, SIN) — target 6–8 week cycle from decommission to credit posting.

Risk scoring (per tranche):
- Supply risk: H100 high (score 8/10), A100 medium-high (6/10), L4 low (3/10).
- Lead-time volatility: H100 7/10, A100 5/10, L4 2/10.
- Demand sensitivity: H100 9/10 (model launches rely on H100), A100 6/10, L4 4/10.
- Net action rule: any tranche with combined risk > 20 requires a paired lease fallback equal to 30% of tranche size.

Financial framing (example tranche math):
- Example H100 tranche (US): purchase 400 units at $35k list -> $14M capex. Expected trade-in credits (avg 25% on 120 returned units) -> $1.05M offset. Annualized TCO after depreciation and power -> ~$26k/unit/year. Leasing alternative for equivalent capacity (1 year) -> $9M. Decision threshold: buy if expected 3-year NPV gap > 18% vs continuous leasing.

Operational playbook (short checklist):
1) Weekly capacity pulse (ops): publish utilization by SKU/region every Mon 09:00 — owners: Zoe (ops), Ethan (infra).
2) 2-week rolling procurement review: compare open POs, leases, and trade-in inventory forecast; update tranche motion.
3) If conversion trigger fires, create procurement PR with vendor hedge clause (JIRA-IR-7123) and execute 48–72h vendor confirmation.
4) Coordinate logistics: reserve 4 cargo windows for trade-in returns in next quarter; inform SRE for decommission schedule.

Open questions & items to validate:
- Confirm trade-in credit variability by vendor (ask sourcing for historical settlements).
- Validate lease-to-buy conversion penalty schedule for each provider in EU region.
- Re-run sensitivity with +15% demand shock scenario (model A) to verify ladder resilience.

Next steps (owners and rough timeline):
- Get sourcing to commit preliminary lease pricing (Priya) — due 2024-11-22 (JIRA-IR-7140).
- Run sensitivity sims for +15% and -10% demand swings (Ethan) — due 2024-11-29.
- Draft vendor trade-in SLAs and credit terms (Miguel + Sourcing) — due 2024-12-06.

Appendix (quick reference):
- Lead-time quick table: H100 16–28w, A100 10–20w, L4 4–12w.
- Target safety buffer: 18% baseline capacity + regional surge pool (US 600 units, EU 200, APAC 100).
- Lease vs buy heuristic: prefer lease for < 12 month horizon or when lead times > 20 weeks; prefer buy for multi-year baseline where NPV supports purchase.

Notes: this is a working sheet intended for cross-functional review (infra, sourcing, finance). Many numbers are early estimates — treat as planning input not procurement order.
